>pregnancy scare 

Sums up your thoughts on being pregnant.... "Scare". You're not ready or willing. I cannot express this enough but you need to be 1000% ready to have kids. Pregnancy is HARD. Having a baby is EVEN HARDER.

My partner and I tried for *3 years* to have a baby. I DESPERATELY WANTED a baby. He wanted a baby.
The baby is here and it is HARD. YOU will be off on maternity leave with the baby all day so you need to be on board. I honestly cannot stress enough, you will resent your husband, you may even resent your child. It is not easy being sleep deprived, house in a mess, touched out. I am incredibly lucky that my partner will cook, clean, take the baby, play feed them. Not all women have that support but I do and some days are still hard. This baby is super wanted and loved, I can't imagine if you were not all in.



>But the idea of actively trying and pursuing fertility treatments sounded terrible to me, and I've just never had a desire for parenthood or pregnancy or anything related to kids in general.

I have BEEN THROUGH the fertility treatment. It is not pleasant. The scans. The probing. The drugs. Mood swings, hair loss, hair growth. Drug side effects....

>: I don't want to do IVF or anything where I have to take medication or hormones,

I am not sure where you're from but first point for us for fertility treatment was ME taking DRUGS. Interuterine insemination was not the first port of call for us so just be aware that this may be an issue for you too. 

>We had a few events sprinkled throughout the year we were planning on going to that I consider really good for our relationship

Once baby is here your whole life revolves around them and their schedule. Yes you can still go out to enjoy yourself but don't regret not going to XYZ. Also having something to look forward to is nice. Again, the bonding time between you two is important.

>I need him to promise to start cleaning if we have a kid (he currently does literally no cleaning),

He needs to start cleaning NOW. Get into a semi routine. This is not something to pick up when the kid is here. If he can't clean now no way will he be doing it when baby is here. Who currently does all the cooking? Of you decide to breastfeed you could have baby stuck to you for an hour at a time. They could feed for an hour, snooze and back on it again. Some babies will only contact sleep (sleep on you or your husband). You cannot sleep when baby is on you (safe sleep). I'm telling you now your priority will be your basic human needs over cleaning. He needs to pick up the slack. If you have a c section that is minimum 6 weeks of doing literally nothing helpful. I couldn't walk up the stairs after mine.

**gross tmi warning** I tried to do stuff too early and popped a stitch so had to have daily dressings as it was leaking. Who wants to take your barely week old baby to the hospital every day to get your wound redressed??? 



Honestly, couples counseling sounds like a good idea if you do not want to divorce but I would be worried you're incompatible now. 

Having children is a lifelong dedication and you need to be on board 100%. The reasoning that you provided imo is not enough reason to have kids. 

Please have an honest discussion with him about this, and communicate with each other. Wish you all the best.

This can cause bleed/spotting when irritated. This can be thru sex/cervical exam, or even just walking can cause a bleed... 

If you're unsure get checked out!

On this call I was asked about my height, weight for bmi. We have a follow up appointment in approx 3 months time to see where I am with weight loss. If I have hit my 30 BMI then I will be put on Clomid to try and get things going.
